judgements.justification: Stage 1 checked every claim it could and found each correct; no score or recommendation rested on a wrong claim about the results.
A's authors conceded positioning faults (fairness out of scope, Lemma 3.1 known), not unfavourable results, and A is the committee that ended lower, not higher than its information supported.
Reviewer_oRvo's Appendix B follow-up came on 2021-08-12 and the authors answered it on 2021-08-19; no objection arrived after the authors could reply.

B's area chair did not cite only scores: it promoted the paper on its own reading ('very strong contribution', broad interest), and A's area chair cited specific concerns, so the split is not a bare threshold difference.
Neither committee had a reviewer whose expert verdict differed from the rest; all ratings lie within one point and confidences are similar.
A's positioning concerns were answered with promised citations and lifted two A scores, while B's answered concerns moved no score; the rebuttal did not widen the gap toward B.
Stage 1 finds no outlier in either committee; all ratings lie within one point.
No reviewer's score stood apart from its committee, so no outlying reviewer existed to ignore the response.
Neither committee had a low-scoring detractor; A's lowest final score is 6 and its area chair did not set one aside.
No reviewer or area chair raised audience breadth or venue fit against the paper; B's area chair instead forecast broad interest.
Both meta-reviews report their reviewers accurately: A's names the concerns its reviewers raised, and B's 'uniformly positive' matches 7, 6, 7, 7, 7.
B's engaged reviewers (Reviewer_ZiMd, Reviewer_dTZk) kept their scores, and B's silent reviewers already rated 7, so unanswered responses did not hold B down or explain the split.
No reviewer on either committee said they could not verify the results; confidences are 3 or 4 on both.
Neither committee split between accept and reject; all ratings are 6 or 7.
Stage 1 notes no difference in substance between the authors' responses to the two committees.
The related work that only A's reviewers found missing does not contradict the paper's novelty, and both committees saw that Lemma 3.1 and importance weighting are standard.
B's area chair stated grounds for the spotlight (its own reading of the contribution and a forecast of broad interest), so the tier was not unexplained.
A's reviewers objected that fairness is never defined, a correct positioning fault, not an objection from a neighbouring field's premises; stage 1 records no field difference.
No reviewer on either committee rated above 7 or argued for the paper beyond acceptance, so neither committee had a champion.
Both committees accepted the paper; neither judged the promised revisions too large for camera-ready.
Both recommendations rest on the visible reviews and meta-reviews; stage 1 records no emergency or off-record input.
Both committees judged the paper as a theory contribution on the same terms; A's faults concern positioning, not a standard tied to contribution type.
No final score is below the accept threshold; A's lowest ratings are 6.
